_comment: Canonical protocol parameters. This file is the single source of truth:
the whitepaper, /tokenomics, /stake and README must quote these numbers,
and contracts/tools/set-params.js is the only thing that puts them on
chain. If you change a number here and nowhere else, the docs are wrong;
if you change it on chain and nowhere else, this file is wrong. Both are

rationale: A 3% fee with 30% of it burned destroys 0.9% of GMV. Against any emission
schedule that is noise: the current design needs USD 33M of annual GMV in
year one just to stop diluting, and USD 133M by year five. No new compute
network does that, so the token was structurally inflationary for its whole
growth phase. The correct description of the old model is not 'a fee-burning
token', it is 'an inflationary token with a rounding-error burn'.
An 8% fee with half of it burned destroys 4.0% of GMV — 4.4x the sink — and
the pitch ('50-70% cheaper than Web2 cloud') still holds with a protocol
take of 8%.
The 30% staker slice is new and is the part that matters most. Previously
stakers were paid exclusively in emissions, so the only reason to stake was
dilution: mercenary capital with no reason to stay. A pro-rata share of fees
is revenue, not inflation, and it is the yield an investor can model.

onChain.note: PROTOCOL_FEE_BPS, FEE_BURN_BPS and FEE_REWARD_BPS are compile-time constants in OMCComputeMarket, so unlike the staking ladder these cannot be changed by an owner transaction. They change at the next deployment.

emission.poolNote: The pool is an allocation ceiling, not a promise to mint. Only 400,000,000 is scheduled; the remaining 100,000,000 is a DAO reserve that cannot be minted before 2037 and requires a governance vote. Scheduling the whole pool forces 60M/year ceilings in the late years purely to make the arithmetic balance.

revenueGate.source: trailing 30-day protocol fee revenue, denominated in OMC, read from OMCComputeMarket
rationale: A schedule answers 'how fast may we spend the pool'. It cannot answer the
question that decides whether the token survives: 'how fast are we spending
it relative to what the network earns'. Tying emission to fee revenue does,
and it does so without a committee: no revenue means no emission, so a
network that never finds demand simply never inflates.
The consequence is worth stating plainly, because it is the whole design.
Inside the gate regime the ratio of burn to emission is exactly
burnShare / k, independent of GMV and of price: 17% in year 1, 25% in
year 2, 33%, 50%, 67%, and 100% from year 6 — at which point emission
equals burn and circulating supply stops growing, whatever the scale.
The schedule then becomes a ceiling that only binds when the network is
genuinely earning, which is the correct place for a ceiling.

emission.implementation: OMCStaking holds a single per-second rate and has no view of the market contract, so the gate needs one of two things: (a) a keeper that calls setEmissionPerSecond monthly with the gated rate, or (b) at mainnet, an EmissionController contract that reads fee revenue from OMCComputeMarket and exposes currentRate(). (b) is the honest one; (a) is acceptable on the testnet only, and only if the keeper's calls are public and auditable.

testnet.note: The deployed testnet contract emits 0.01 tOMC/s (about 864 a day) as a test rate. It is not the schedule above: tOMC is not OMC, has no cap and has no value. /stake shows whatever the contract currently pays, read live.

staking.rationale: A stake is collateral, and collateral only deters if it is worth more than the damage an operator can do. A fixed OMC figure is a fixed dollar figure only on the day it is written; when the token falls 80% the deterrent falls with it. Tier minimums are therefore denominated in USD and restated in OMC at each re-peg, so the bond keeps its size while the token price moves.
staking.unstakeRationale: The deployed contract lets a node unstake in the same block it registers, which makes staking a free option: stake, accrue emissions for a week, unstake, sell. With a 20% APR and instant exit there is no cost to trying, so the marginal staker is a yield farmer rather than an operator, and the emissions meant to buy capacity buy nothing but sell pressure. A 14-day cooldown makes the position a commitment: long enough that farming is a real risk, short enough that an honest operator is not locked out of hardware resale.

tiers.hardware: Consumer GPU, up to 24 GB VRAM (RTX 3090 / 4090 class)
Workstation / professional GPU (RTX A6000, L40S class)
Data-center GPU, 80 GB class (A100 / H100 single card)

repeg.rule: Restate the ladder when the 30-day volume-weighted average price leaves a +/-25% band around the reference price used at the last restatement. The OMC amounts stored on chain are authoritative; /stake reads them live and never caches a copy.

onChain.note: The deployed testnet contract runs placeholder amounts because tOMC has no price to anchor to. They are not the published ladder; the USD targets above are. contracts/tools/set-params.js ladder --apply replaces them.

airdrop.vestingRationale: 2% of supply released to whoever claims first is a day-one sell wall built by the project itself, and the wallets that dump are the ones least likely to ever run a GPU. A 25/75 split keeps the claim meaningful — you can do something with it immediately — while removing the cliff that market makers price in.
airdrop.note: 100 OMC is the maximum a single wallet can register. Against a $250 tier-1 bond that is worth 40% of a tier-1 stake only if OMC trades at $2.50; the free-stake loop that a fixed 20/100/500/1000/5000 ladder produced therefore closes as a side effect of USD pricing, without a separate lock.

capital.reservedNote: Institutional 10% + private 8%. No round has been closed, so there is no price and no discount to disclose — which is itself the disclosure. An 18% allocation sitting in a table with no price against it is the most common reason a token diligence stops early.
disclosureRequiredBeforeAnyRound: Amount raised and the FDV it was raised at
Lock-up and vesting per round (proposed floor: 12-month cliff, 36-month linear)
Whether any allocation carries a discount or a liquidation preference
Treasury address and the multisig threshold controlling it
Legal entity, jurisdiction, and whether the token is characterised as a security there
